summary: 9remote spawns a network-attached PTY shell reachable over a Cloudflare tunnel
details: The package's server component (dist/server.cjs) launches a PTY daemon via node-pty that spawns the host's default shell (bash/zsh/sh/cmd/powershell) and wires the PTY's stdin to messages received over a Socket.IO/WebRTC bridge, with the endpoint exposed to the public internet through a Cloudflare tunnel and clients connecting via https://9remote.cc. Any peer that completes the QR-code pairing gains an interactive shell on the installer's machine with the privileges of the user running the CLI. The postinstall step also materializes a second node_modules tree at ~/.9remote/runtime by running `npm install systray2@2.1.4 --no-save` from the public npm registry; this is a pinned registry install of a legitimate tray helper, but it leaves persistent files in the user's home directory outside normal npm uninstall tracking. The advertised purpose of the package is exactly this remote-shell behavior, but the resulting capability is a full-host remote code execution surface on any machine where the CLI is run.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
